reviews.hedge_rule_note: Hedge rule passes, and this entry is one of the better applications of it on the page. The list fragments ("Kabbalistic Malkuth fixed.", "Alchemical fixed Earth.", "Rosicrucian dome symbolism.") are set beside the proximate source's actual text (Hall 1928) and beside the traditions' own texts, and the refutation answers those, not the fragments: Hall's sephirothic table, Hall's Welling plate, Norton's fixation definition as Hall prints it, Duncan's and Webb's catechisms, the Fama's own inscription, Ulansey and Beck. compression.assessed=True with drifted=True is honest, list_phrasing and source_wording are both populated with real text, and the note refuses to force the equivocation drift (166/178/djed) into the seven-value enum, per the harness's own instruction. Item 461 is excluded rather than guessed at, and the denominator is restated as eleven. Two caveats that do NOT overturn the verdict but should be recorded: (i) the compression note asserts "Nothing was misquoted anywhere in this cluster" while the same block correctly classifies item 165 as unsourced_addition — those are compatible (addition is not misquotation) but the sentence reads as broader than it is; (ii) our own refutation commits, in miniature, two of the faults the hedge rule polices — it adds "seven-sided for the seven planets" to the Fama, which the Fama does not say, and it identifies a specific Hall plate as "the diagram behind item 458" without evidence from the list. Those are logged as holes below rather than as a hedge-rule failure, because the refutation's aim is at the source throughout.
reviews.summary: The argument is substantively sound and its hedge-rule work is exemplary; the verdict UNFALSIFIABLE should stand, and every substantive quotation from Hall, Duncan, Webb, Mackey, Blavatsky, the Fama, Malkuth, Boaz/Jachin, the djed and the liturgical-east convention checked out verbatim against the primary sources. But the entry's §10 and compression note still describe our own record in the present tense as uncorrected — "Our record names Helena Blavatsky ... as the head of this cluster", "Our basis line reads: Blavatsky's claimed source text, the Book of Dzyan..." — when clusters.py was corrected on 2026-08-07 and now reads Hall/1928 with the Dzyan sentence withdrawn; the published card therefore contradicts its own body. Worse, the corrected originator string "Manly P. Hall; Helena Blavatsky" is not a key in build.py's ORIGINATOR_PID map, so the live card renders "no named originator" one line above a TLDR that calls Blavatsky "the originator our record names", and the site's own statistics now disagree with themselves by exactly D07's twelve items (items_traceable_to_a_named_originator 372 vs 461 minus 101 untraced by lineage = 360).
citation_failures: scripts/_b6_D07.py sources[3] cites sacred-texts sta37 for BOTH the fixation definition and "the subtle spirit will rise and be gone". The second phrase is not in sta37. It is in sta38 (Part Two), and it is not Hall's: Hall introduces it as "The philosopher of Leyden continues", an anonymous 1662 deathbed alchemical testament he is quoting. Our text says Hall "warns the operator".

sta37's fixation definition is not Hall's own glossary. Hall introduces it: "In his Key to Alchemy, Samuel Norton divides into fourteen parts the processes or states through which the alchemical substances pass" - the definition is Norton's twelfth entry. Our refutation says the source "says the same thing in its own glossary", and the module docstring says "Hall's own glossary".

The Fama quotations are dated "(1614)" but taken from sacred-texts sro/rhr/rhr06, which is Waite's 1887 reprint of Thomas Vaughan's 1652 English translation, and which dates the first printing to 1616, not 1614. The English wording we quote is Vaughan's, not the 1614 German text's.

en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Djed is cited to support "No astronomical or cosmographic sense of the sign is attested", but that same article carries Cohen and Kangas's reading that "for both Osiris and Enki, an erect pole or polelike symbol stands beneath a celestial symbol".

The Teresa of Avila quotations are cited to an undated blog post (thecontemplativelife.org) that names no translator and no edition, for a text we date 1577 (composition; first published 1588). Quotes verified verbatim against that page, but the provenance chain stops there.

UNCHECKED, not failed: the specimen list at withthesun33.com/about-1 was not re-fetched this run, so the claim that a particular Hall plate stands "behind item 458" could not be tested against the list itself. UNCHECKED, not failed: English tracing-board ritual texts (masonslibrary.org, masoniclibrary.org.au, camden704.org.uk) all returned ROBOTS_DISALLOWED, so item 459's named artefact could not be verified this run.

holes.quoted_phrase: Our record names Helena Blavatsky and
holes.description: Section 10 describes our own record in the present tense as still uncorrected, and it is not. scripts/clusters.py D07 now reads originator="Manly P. Hall; Helena Blavatsky", originator_work="The Secret Teachings of All Ages (1928); Isis Unveiled (1877)", year="1928", and its note contains no Dzyan sentence; review/corrections.json logs the change at 2026-08-07. So the published card states the corrected record at the top and, six screens down, tells the reader that our record says the opposite and that the Dzyan sentence 'is wrong ... and is corrected in full below'. On a page whose Method tab sells our willingness to correct ourselves, a self-criticism section that has not noticed its own correction is the single most damaging thing on this entry, and a defender only has to scroll.
holes.recommendation: Replace the opening of section 10 with: "10. Where our own record was wrong, and where the list contradicts itself. Two things must be said against ourselves before anything is said against the list, and both have already been acted on. First, the originator. Our record named Helena Blavatsky and Isis Unveiled (1877) as the head of this cluster until 7 August 2026. It now names Manly Hall and 1928 primary — the twelve items track his chapter list and his subtitle — with Blavatsky secondary, as the source of the framing idea that one wisdom underlies every tradition. Second, and more seriously, the Book of Dzyan sentence that stood in our basis line until the same date was wrong in three separate ways. It has been withdrawn, and the reasoning is set out in full below. Now the list."

holes.quoted_phrase: Our basis line reads
holes.description: Same staleness, in the compression note, twice. 'Our basis line reads: "Blavatsky's claimed source text, the Book of Dzyan, is regarded by Buddhist-studies scholars as her own invention."' - it does not; that sentence was removed from clusters.py on 2026-08-07 and the note now reads 'Esoteric interpretive literature. Where these traditions do carry cosmology it is the geocentric nested spheres of their own century...'. Two paragraphs later, 'The originator pairing should be reversed. Our record makes Blavatsky and Isis Unveiled (1877) primary and Hall secondary' - it has been reversed and it does not. Both recommendations are written as outstanding work that is in fact complete, which understates the project and misdescribes the artefact.

Where these traditions do carry cosmology it is the geocentric nested spheres of their own century - which contain a spherical Earth. Hall captions the Rosicrucian plate a Ptolemaic chart." If the Dzyan question is wanted at all it belongs on the Blavatsky biography, stated as a search that has not found its object rather than as a charge.' Change the heading of the second sub-finding from 'The originator pairing should be reversed.' to 'The originator pairing has been reversed.' and its first sentence to 'Our record made Blavatsky and Isis Unveiled (1877) primary and Hall secondary until 7 August 2026.'

holes.description: The corrected originator string is not a key in build.py's ORIGINATOR_PID map (which still carries only the pre-correction "Helena Blavatsky; Manly P. Hall": "PER-BLAVATSKY"). Verified by running the build: arguments['ARG-D07']['originator_id'] is None. Two live consequences. (1) The rendered card in docs/index.html reads 'no named originator' in its meta line, one line above a TLDR that says 'Helena Blavatsky, the originator our record names'. Hall\": \"PER-HALL\"," with "    \"Helena Blavatsky; Manly P. Hall\": \"PER-BLAVATSKY\",\n    \"Manly P. Hall; Helena Blavatsky\": \"PER-HALL\", \"Manly P. Hall\": \"PER-HALL\"," and rebuild. holes.quoted_phrase: will rise and be gone
holes.description: Section 2 writes: Hall 'gives fixation as "the act or process of ceasing to be a fluid and becoming firm; state of being fixed", and warns the operator that otherwise "the subtle spirit will rise and be gone"'. Neither clause is Hall in his own voice, and the second is not at the URL we cite. The fixation definition is Samuel Norton's - Hall introduces it 'In his Key to Alchemy, Samuel Norton divides into fourteen parts the processes or states through which the alchemical substances pass' (sacred-texts sta37). 'The subtle spirit will rise and be gone' is in sta38, Part Two, inside a quotation Hall introduces as 'The philosopher of Leyden continues', an anonymous 1662 alchemical testament about storing dew. Attributing to a named author words he is quoting is the exact quote-provenance failure the harness lists under biography checks, and here it is done to the cluster's own proximate source. It also costs us evidence: Norton (Key to Alchemy, 16th c.) and a 1662 practitioner are better witnesses to the technical meaning of 'fixed' than a 1928 populariser.
holes.recommendation: Replace that sentence with: "The list’s own cited source prints the definition and does not dispute it: Hall, in The Theory and Practice of Alchemy, reproduces Samuel Norton’s fourteen-part scheme from the Key to Alchemy, whose twelfth process is fixation, “the act or process of ceasing to be a fluid and becoming firm; state of being fixed”; and the second part of the same chapter prints a 1662 practitioner’s warning that unless the vessel is kept cool and sealed “the subtle spirit will rise and be gone”." Add to sources: dict(label="Hall, “The Theory and Practice of Alchemy” Part Two — the philosopher of Leyden, “the subtle spirit will rise and be gone”", url="https://sacred-texts.com/eso/sta/sta38.htm").

holes.quoted_phrase: diagram behind item 458 is captioned, in the list's own source, a Ptolemaic chart
holes.description: This asserts which of Hall's fifteen Rosicrucian plates the list means by item 458, and nothing supports the identification. Item 458 reads 'Rosicrucian temple diagrams: cosmos around sanctum'; the plate we point at is Table I, Figure 1, an elemental chart with no sanctum in it. Hall's same chapter contains a much better match that our entry never mentions: Table IV, Figure 53, which Hall says 'has been designated the symbolic tomb of Christian Rosencreutz', described with concentric divine spheres, zodiacal correspondences and planetary orbits around a centre (sacred-texts sta35). Our own refutation section 5 already treats 458 as the tomb/vault ('Items 170 and 458: the Rosicrucian vault says what it is'), so the entry identifies item 458 with two different plates in two places. And section 9 makes a virtue of refusing to guess at item 461's truncated wording while the TLDR guesses which diagram 458 denotes - the same fault, in the field readers see first. The finding survives the fix; only the pinpointing has to go.
holes.recommendation: In the TLDR replace 'The Rosicrucian diagram behind item 458 is captioned, in the list’s own source, a Ptolemaic chart' with 'The first of the fifteen Rosicrucian diagrams Hall prints is captioned, by Hall, a Ptolemaic chart, and the one he calls the tomb of Christian Rosencreutz is drawn as concentric planetary spheres'. Make the same change in verdict_challenge ('the Rosicrucian diagram behind item 458 is captioned in the list’s own source as a Ptolemaic chart' becomes 'the first of Hall’s Rosicrucian plates is captioned by him as a Ptolemaic chart'), and in the compression source_wording label ('on the plate behind item 458' becomes 'Table I, Figure 1'). In section 5, after 'its earth has a surface, a subterranean air and a central fire', add: 'And the plate Hall actually attaches to the vault says the same thing: Table IV, Figure 53, which he calls “the symbolic tomb of Christian Rosencreutz”, is drawn as concentric spheres with zodiacal correspondences and planetary orbits about a centre.'

holes.quoted_phrase: Hall describes Table I as
holes.description: Wrong locator. Hall's sentence is 'Figure 1 is a Ptolemaic chart showing the true relationship existing between the primordial elements' (sacred-texts sta35). Table I contains Figures 1 to 11; the caption belongs to Figure 1, not to the whole table. The ring inventory that follows in our gloss - Schamayim, the seven Spiritual Intelligences, subtle air, the surface of the earth and sea, the subterranean air, the central fire - is likewise Figure 1's, and is accurate to it.
holes.recommendation: Replace 'Hall describes Table I as “a Ptolemaic chart' with 'Of the first figure on Table I, Hall writes that it is “a Ptolemaic chart'.

holes.quoted_phrase: in its own glossary
holes.description: The fixation definition is not Hall's glossary, in his own or any other sense: Hall is reprinting Samuel Norton's fourteen alchemical processes from the Key to Alchemy (sacred-texts sta37). The module docstring compounds it - 'Hall's own glossary in "The Theory and Practice of Alchemy" gives it as "ceasing to be a fluid and becoming firm"'. A defender who opens the page finds the attribution wrong in the one place where we are quoting the list's own authority against it.
holes.recommendation: Replace 'The list’s own cited source says the same thing in its own glossary: Hall, in The Theory and Practice of Alchemy, gives fixation as' with 'The list’s own cited source prints the same thing: Hall, in The Theory and Practice of Alchemy, reproduces Samuel Norton’s fourteen alchemical processes from the Key to Alchemy, whose twelfth is fixation,'. Correct the module docstring line to 'Samuel Norton’s Key to Alchemy, printed in Hall’s alchemy chapter, gives fixation as "ceasing to be a fluid and becoming firm".'

holes.quoted_phrase: seven-sided for the seven planets
holes.description: Presented inside a list of things the Fama itself says ('The text is not being coy. It says the room is a compendium, an epitome, a scale model made by hand, with an artificial sun in the ceiling ..., seven-sided for the seven planets, built so that ...'). The Fama does not say it. Checked directly against the text we cite: the vault's seven sides and seven corners are given with their dimensions and the sides are divided into ten squares, but no planetary gloss is attached to the number anywhere in the description. The planetary reading is a later commentators' inference. Everything else in that sentence is verbatim in the source, which is precisely why the one addition stands out - it is an unsourced_addition in a paragraph whose whole force is that the source states its own meaning.
holes.recommendation: Replace 'seven-sided for the seven planets, built so that' with 'seven-sided and seven-cornered, built so that'. If the planetary reading is wanted, add it separately and mark it: 'Later commentators read the seven sides as the seven planets; the Fama itself attaches no gloss to the number.'

holes.quoted_phrase: Fama Fraternitatis (1614)
holes.description: Edition and translation precision - this project's signature failure mode, per three of the thirteen logged corrections. The English we quote ('a vault of seven sides and seven corners, every side five foot broad, and the height of eight foot'; 'they might by this onely vault be restored again') is Thomas Vaughan's 1652 translation as reprinted by A. E. Waite in 1887, which is the page in our sources list. The 1614 Fama is German. Worse for us, the page we cite dates the first printing to 1616, so a defender checking our footnote finds a different year on it than the one in our text. 1614 is the right date for the Fama's first printing; the problem is that we present a 1652 English text as if it were the 1614 one and cite a page that disagrees about the year.
holes.recommendation: Replace 'Fama Fraternitatis (1614): “a vault of seven sides' with 'Fama Fraternitatis (Cassel, 1614; quoted here in Thomas Vaughan’s 1652 English, the version in general circulation): “a vault of seven sides'. Update the sources label to 'Fama Fraternitatis, Vaughan’s 1652 English text of the vault of C.R.C. — in Waite, The Real History of the Rosicrucians (1887), ch. III' and the compression source_wording label likewise.

holes.quoted_phrase: Malkuth is not called fixed by anybody
holes.description: A universal negative in a section heading, backed by two sources (Hall's chapter and the Malkuth Wikipedia article). Both checks are good - 'fixed' genuinely does not occur in either - but the heading claims vastly more than they establish, and the body extends it further to 'or in the Jewish sources', an unbounded corpus we did not search and cannot search. The obvious counter-move is the Hermetic Qabalah literature, where Malkuth's four quarters are conventionally assigned the Kerubim, i.e. the four fixed signs; whether or not that is what the list meant, it is a place where the word 'fixed' sits next to Malkuth, and one produced example destroys a claim phrased as 'by anybody'. The argument does not need the absolute: the point that the word is an addition survives being scoped.
holes.recommendation: Change the heading to '3. Item 165: nothing in the standard descriptions of Malkuth calls it fixed.' and change 'The word fixed does not appear in that description, in Hall’s treatment, or in the Jewish sources.' to 'The word fixed appears neither in that description nor anywhere in Hall’s treatment of Malchuth. If a source for it exists in the later Hermetic Qabalah, the list does not cite one, and the burden is theirs.'

holes.quoted_phrase: which sefirah in that scheme owns the fixed stars
holes.description: Hall's table does not use the phrase 'fixed stars' anywhere; Chochmah's entry in the THE UNIVERSE column reads 'The Zodiac' (verified verbatim, sacred-texts sta29). Identifying the zodiacal sphere with the sphere of the fixed stars is correct Ptolemaic astronomy, but it is our inference, and we present it as something to be read off Hall's scheme - two sentences after telling the reader that the word 'fixed' appears nowhere in Hall's treatment. As written, the paragraph appears to source the word 'fixed' to a table that does not contain it, in the course of objecting that the list sourced the word 'fixed' to a tradition that does not contain it.
holes.recommendation: Replace 'Note also which sefirah in that scheme owns the fixed stars. It is Chochmah, at the top of the tree — the fixity in the Kabbalistic cosmos is a property of the stars, and it is the highest thing in the diagram, not the lowest.' with 'Note also where the eighth sphere lands in that scheme. Hall gives Chochmah, the second sefirah, “The Zodiac” — which in the Ptolemaic order it reproduces is the sphere of the fixed stars. Whatever is fixed in this cosmos is fixed near the top of the diagram, not at the bottom.'

holes.quoted_phrase: Items 452 and 459: the Masonic sources answer this themselves
holes.description: Item 459 is 'Masonic tracing boards beneath starry canopy', and the section never reaches a tracing board. It answers from the first-degree catechism in Duncan's (1866) and the fellowcraft lecture in Webb (1797/1808) - both American monitors, neither of which is a tracing board, an artefact belonging chiefly to the English lodge tradition and carrying its own ritual Explanation. The answer we give is almost certainly the right one, and the Webb globes material is devastating, but we are answering an adjacent artefact, which is the fault logged against ourselves in corrections.json for ARG-E03 ('We pointed readers at the artefact with the least of the argument in it'). Note: the English tracing-board ritual texts could not be reached this run - three sites returned ROBOTS_DISALLOWED - so the replacement below deliberately does not quote one.
holes.recommendation: After the Duncan's paragraph, insert: 'A note on the artefact. Item 459 names tracing boards, which are an English lodge form rather than the American monitors quoted here, and which carry their own ritual Explanation. We answer from the monitors because their glosses are printed and checkable; if a defender wants the tracing-board Explanation put in evidence instead, we will take it, because the board it explains is the one whose second-degree companion carries the pair of globes described below.'

holes.quoted_phrase: No astronomical or cosmographic sense of the sign is attested
holes.description: Overstated absolute, and contradicted on the very page we cite for it. The Djed article we list as a source carries: 'Cohen and Kangas suggest that the tree is probably associated with the Sumerian god of male fertility, Enki and that for both Osiris and Enki, an erect pole or polelike symbol stands beneath a celestial symbol' - a cosmic-axis reading, which is cosmographic in the ordinary sense of that word. It is comparative mythology and it does not make the djed a claim about the earth's motion, so conceding it costs us nothing; leaving the absolute standing hands a defender a one-click refutation of a sentence we did not need.
holes.recommendation: Replace 'No astronomical or cosmographic sense of the sign is attested.' with 'Where the comparative literature does read the djed cosmically — Cohen and Kangas take the pole under a celestial symbol as a shared Osiris-Enki motif — the sense is axis and support, not the earth’s state of motion. No Egyptian source makes the sign a statement about whether the earth moves.'

holes.quoted_phrase: nine rungs
holes.description: Arithmetic. Chochmah is the second sefirah and Malchuth the tenth in Hall's table (verified verbatim, sacred-texts sta29), so the distance is eight, not nine. The error appears twice: 'The list has moved the word down nine rungs' in section 3, and 'nine rungs higher, at Chochmah' in the compression note. Nine would be the distance from Kether.
holes.recommendation: In section 3 change 'The list has moved the word down nine rungs.' to 'The list has moved the word down eight rungs.' In the compression note change 'belongs to the fixed stars, nine rungs higher, at Chochmah' to 'belongs to the eighth sphere, eight rungs higher, at Chochmah'.

holes.quoted_phrase: Teresa of Ávila, Interior Castle (1577), First Mansions
holes.description: The three Teresa quotations verify verbatim against the page we cite, but that page is an undated blog post naming no translator and no edition, and we date the work 1577 (the year of composition; first publication was 1588). For a project that has logged three separate corrections about edition dating, quoting a sixteenth-century primary text through a blog with no edition statement is the weakest link in the sources list.
holes.recommendation: Replace the source entry with one naming an edition, e.g. dict(label="Teresa of Ávila, The Interior Castle (written 1577; first published 1588), First Mansions ch. 1 — the castle of a single diamond, the chiefest mansion at the centre; Benedictines of Stanbrook / Zimmerman translation", url="https://www.ccel.org/ccel/teresa/castle2.i.html"), and in section 8 change 'opens the Interior Castle (1577)' to 'opens the Interior Castle (written 1577, published 1588)'.

reviews.hedge_rule_note: FAILS. Our compression block holds the ten list items against a 27-word distributor's marketing synopsis (In Ohm Entertainment, PR Newswire, 25 March 2015) and calls that "the source". But our own published cluster record names the source as Galileo Was Wrong (7th ed., 2013), Vol. I ch. 3 and Vol. II ch. 10, and our own gloss says "Sungenis and Bennett's Galileo Was Wrong is the source of the CMB material". The book is never quoted, never cited in E01's twelve sources, and never compared to anything. We audited one compression against another compression. Second failure, on the rule's second clause: the gloss asserts the book "is more hedged than the claims descending from it" — the exact finding the rule says must be demonstrated and published — and then demonstrates nothing. Third: the recorded drift is not earned. drift_type="hedge_dropped" rests on the note "The list states as fact what the film puts as a question", but the synopsis sentence we ourselves quote (verified verbatim against the press release) is a flat declarative — "surveys that disclose unexpected evidence of a preferred direction in the cosmos, aligned with our supposedly insignificant Earth". The "What if everything you think you know about our Universe is wrong?" line is a separate opening tagline, not a hedge on that sentence. Against the item "CMB axis aligned with Earth.", the source asserts precisely that, so on this comparand the honest drift_type is `none`. Mitigating: the refutation itself does target the film's own words rather than the list fragment, and does so explicitly ("The synopsis performs the entire slide in one phrase"). The failure is that it targets the wrong artefact — the most compressed one available — not that it targets a fragment of the right one.
reviews.summary: E01's physics is sound, its steelman is genuine KERNEL tier, and the MISLEADING verdict survives — the axis-is-not-a-centre argument is decisive and independent of everything below. But three critical defects sit on top of it: a quotation attributed to Planck 2018 VII five times, including in the TLDR, that I could not locate in that paper (or in Planck 2015 XVI, or in Schwarz et al. 2016); a hedge-rule audit run against the film's press-release blurb while our own record names Galileo Was Wrong as the source, which is never cited or quoted anywhere in the entry; and the 2026-08-08 E03 correction applied to the wrong cluster — E01's record now carries E03's corrected originator_work and E03's justifying comment about dark flow and item 327, while E03 still reads "The Principle (film)", 2014, uncorrected, in the published data file. Fifteen other citations checked out verbatim, including every quote from Land & Magueijo 2005 and 2007, Schwarz et al. 2004 and 2016, Copi et al. 2009, de Oliveira-Costa et al. 2004, Bennett et al. 2011, Patel et al. 2025, the press-release synopsis and the Mulgrew disavowal.
citation_failures: Planck 2018 VII (arXiv:1906.02552 / A&A 641:A7) — the word "uncontested" could not be located. Checked the A&A full HTML, the ar5iv render, and the arXiv PDF (coverage ran title page through §5.5.1; §7 Conclusions not reachable). Also absent from Planck 2015 XVI and from Schwarz et al. 2016 (whose PDF I could search successfully — it returned the neighbouring quotes but not this one). Marked FAILED rather than unchecked because three independent renderings of the cited paper returned nothing, and the paper's Introduction says close to the opposite: "A conservative explanation for the temperature anomalies is that they are simply statistical flukes" and "the generally modest level of significance claimed".

Planck 2018 VII — "given the modest significances at which they deviate from the standard ΛCDM cosmological model, and the a posteriori nature of their detection, the extent to which they provide evidence for a violation of isotropy in the CMB remains unclear" — same searches, not located. The paper's Introduction has "the role of a posteriori choices (also referred to as the 'look-elsewhere effect')", which is verified, but not this sentence.

Rick DeLano, "is not about geocentrism per se, but is instead an in-depth cinematic examination of the Copernican Principle itself" — the quote is REAL and verified (statement of 9 April 2014, reproduced at magisterialfundies.blogspot.com), but it appears in no source in E01's source list, and our compression block presents it as though it came from the same press release, which it does not.

UNCHECKED, not failed: Slate, Krauss, 8 April 2014 — Krauss's objection is independently corroborated but I did not fetch the Slate piece to confirm the date. UNCHECKED: whether Galileo Was Wrong Vol. I ch. 3 / Vol. II ch. 10 contains axis-of-evil (as opposed to dipole) material — the archive scan was not re-searched in this pass.

holes.quoted_phrase: Planck's own isotropy paper calls the existence of these features “uncontested”
holes.description: The single most load-bearing quotation in the entry cannot be located in the paper it is attributed to. It appears five times: in the TLDR, in the steelman ("Planck 2018 VII agrees “the existence of these features is uncontested”"), in the straw_man block ("Planck 2018 VII calls their existence uncontested"), in the refutation ("Planck 2018 VII is more even-handed: the features' existence is uncontested, but…"), and in the advocate preemptive ("note Planck itself calls the features' existence uncontested"). I searched Planck 2018 VII in three renderings — the A&A full HTML, the ar5iv HTML, and the arXiv PDF — and the word does not occur in any of them; the PDF pass covered title page through §5.5.1, so §7 Conclusions remains unreachable, but the abstract and Introduction, where such a summary judgement would live, both lack it. It is also absent from Planck 2015 XVI and from Schwarz et al. 2016 (whose PDF I searched successfully, since it returned the adjacent quotes we use). The companion quote in the same refutation sentence — "given the modest significances… the extent to which they provide evidence for a violation of isotropy in the CMB remains unclear" — is likewise unlocatable. This is the rhetorical hinge of the whole entry: the point is that even the sceptical mainstream paper concedes the features are real. Attributed to Schwarz, Copi, Huterer and Starkman it would carry no such weight, and attributed to nobody it is a fabricated citation on a site whose product is other people's citation hygiene. Compounding it, Planck 2018 VII's Introduction says something closer to the opposite — "A conservative explanation for the temperature anomalies is that they are simply statistical flukes" — so a defender who opens the paper finds not silence but tension.
holes.recommendation: Replace the TLDR opening with the verified abstract sentence: "The large-angle CMB alignments are real, reproducible, and still unexplained: Planck's own isotropy paper reports that its data “confirm the presence of several so-called ‘anomalies’ on large angular scales”, and serious cosmologists continue to argue in print that something needs explaining." In the steelman, replace "Planck 2018 VII agrees “the existence of these features is uncontested”." with: "Planck 2018 VII, no friend of the anomaly camp, nevertheless reports that its data “confirm the presence of several so-called ‘anomalies’ on large angular scales”." In straw_man, replace "Planck 2018 VII calls their existence uncontested," with "Planck 2018 VII confirms the presence of several so-called anomalies on large angular scales,". In the advocate preemptive, replace "note Planck itself calls the features' existence uncontested" with "note Planck itself confirms the presence of the features". In the refutation, replace the sentence "Planck 2018 VII is more even-handed: the features' existence is uncontested, but “given the modest significances at which they deviate from the standard ΛCDM cosmological model, and the a posteriori nature of their detection, the extent to which they provide evidence for a violation of isotropy in the CMB remains unclear”." with: "Planck 2018 VII is more even-handed. It confirms the presence of the anomalies while naming the two reasons for caution in its own Introduction: “A conservative explanation for the temperature anomalies is that they are simply statistical flukes”, an explanation it calls “particularly appealing given the generally modest level of significance claimed, and the role of a posteriori choices (also referred to as the ‘look-elsewhere effect’)”." If someone subsequently reaches §7 and finds "uncontested" there, restore it with a section-level locator; until then it must not appear.

holes.quoted_phrase: The list states as fact what the film puts as a question.
holes.description: The hedge-rule audit was run against the wrong artefact, and the drift it records is contradicted by the passage printed beside it. (a) Wrong artefact: source_wording is a 27-word distributor's marketing synopsis, while our own published cluster record names the source as "Galileo Was Wrong (7th ed., 2013), Vol. I ch. 3 and Vol. II ch. 10" and our own gloss says the book "is the source of the CMB material". The book appears nowhere in E01 — not in the twelve sources, not in a single quotation. We compared a compression to a compression and published the result as a provenance finding. Our own E03 work (_b7_E03.py) proves the book is searchable: that agent read the front matter of the seventh edition and located thirteen numbered "Claims and Responses" on the CMB. Nobody did that for the axis of evil. (b) The drift is not earned. I fetched the press release and verified the synopsis verbatim: "surveys that disclose unexpected evidence of a preferred direction in the cosmos, aligned with our supposedly insignificant Earth" — a flat declarative. The "What if everything you think you know about our Universe is wrong?" line is confirmed present but is the release's opening tagline, not a qualifier on that sentence. So against the item "CMB axis aligned with Earth." the source asserts exactly that, and drift_type="hedge_dropped" is asserted against a hedge our own quote shows is not there. A well-informed defender goes straight here: you accused the list of dropping a hedge, and the hedge you say it dropped is a movie poster line.
holes.recommendation: Rewrite the compression block as follows. drift_type="unsourced_addition". source_wording: keep the verified synopsis sentence but label it "the distributor's synopsis — the most compressed form of the argument, not its source". note: "Three of the ten items — CMB axis aligned with Earth, Anisotropy toward Earth, Cosmic anisotropy Earth-oriented — restate the distributor's synopsis at its own strength. On those the wording does not drift: the synopsis asserts a preferred direction in the cosmos, aligned with our supposedly insignificant Earth as fact, and the list says the same thing shorter. The drift is elsewhere. Planck data Earth preference attributes to the Planck mission a finding no Planck paper states and the film does not claim; it is an addition made downstream of everything in the chain. And the film's producer scoped the film narrower than any of the items do: asked directly on 9 April 2014, Rick DeLano said “The Principle”, as the title indicates, is not about geocentrism per se, but is instead an in-depth cinematic examination of the Copernican Principle itself, while adding that any film about the Copernican Principle that does not involve an examination of geocentrism is a fatally flawed film. What we have not done, and record here as an open gap rather than a verdict: the source of record for this cluster is Sungenis and Bennett's Galileo Was Wrong, and no item here has been held against the book's own sentences. Until that comparison is made, the hedge rule has been applied only to the film's marketing copy, which is a derivative of the source and not the source." Then either make the book comparison and rewrite this block properly, or log the gap on the coverage count.

holes.quoted_phrase: Galileo Was Wrong (7th ed., 2013), Vol. I ch. 3 and Vol. II ch. 10
holes.description: The correction logged in corrections.json on 2026-08-08 was applied to the wrong cluster, and the error is live in the published data file. That entry reads: where = "scripts/clusters.py ARG-E03 - originator_work", old = "The Principle (film)", 2014, new = the Galileo Was Wrong chapters. In scripts/clusters.py, E01 now carries that new value together with a comment block whose entire evidence is E03's: "the dipole argument is TEXTUAL, not filmic", "'dark flow' and 'bulk flow' occur ZERO times in all three volumes", "item 327 traces to DeLano's blog, 18 May 2013". Item 327 is an E03 item; the dipole is E03's subject; E01 is the axis of evil. Meanwhile E03's own record is untouched: originator_work="The Principle (film)", year="2014". I confirmed this propagated to the artefact — data/flat-earth-origins-provenance.json has ARG-E01 originator_work = "Galileo Was Wrong (7th ed., 2013), Vol. I ch. 3 and Vol. II ch. 10" and ARG-E03 = "The Principle (film)". So the published genealogy currently attributes E03's provenance to E01 and leaves E03 pointing at the artefact our own correction says contains the least of the argument. On a site whose product is provenance, and whose corrections list is its strongest credential, a correction landing on the wrong row is the worst available failure mode. It also produces a visible self-contradiction inside E01: the cluster says the source is a 2013 book, the DEEP passage cites work="WRK-PRINCIPLE-2014" and quotes a 2015 press release.
holes.recommendation: Move the correction to E03. In scripts/clusters.py set E03 to originator_work="Galileo Was Wrong (7th ed., 2013), Vol. I ch. 3 and Vol. II ch. 10", year="2013", and attach the existing comment block ("Corrected 2026-08-08: the dipole argument is TEXTUAL, not filmic… item 327 traces to DeLano's blog, 18 May 2013") to E03, where its evidence lives. Restore E01 to originator="Robert Sungenis & Rick DeLano", originator_work="The Principle (film)", year="2014", and add the comment: "# 2026-08-09: the 2026-08-08 Galileo Was Wrong correction belonged to E03 and was applied here in error; reverted. The upstream book chapter for the AXIS material (as distinct from the dipole material) has not been checked against the scan. Until it is, the film is the documented source and the book link is an open question, recorded in the compression block." Then append a fourteenth entry to review/corrections.json recording that a published correction was filed against the wrong cluster and both records were wrong for a day.

holes.quoted_phrase: The CMB was emitted about 380,000 years ago
holes.description: Flatly wrong, by about 13.8 billion years, and it opens the paragraph the entry itself treats as the emotional centre of the argument ("Sit with what that means"). The CMB was emitted about 380,000 years AFTER the Big Bang, i.e. roughly 13.8 billion years ago. The rest of the same sentence proves it is a slip rather than a belief — "a gas cloud that collapsed roughly nine billion years after that light departed" is correct only on the 13.8 Gyr reading — but the sentence as published says what it says. This is the single easiest screenshot a defender can take from the page: a site auditing other people's cosmology writing that the microwave background was emitted 380,000 years ago. It also undercuts the paragraph's own argument, which depends on the enormous temporal gap between last scattering and the formation of the ecliptic.
holes.recommendation: Replace with: "The CMB was emitted about 380,000 years after the Big Bang, some 13.8 billion years ago, from a surface some 45 billion light years away in comoving terms."

holes.quoted_phrase: is the source of the CMB material and, as with their Michelson–Gale treatment, is more hedged than the claims descending from it
holes.description: An uncited claim about the contents of a specific in-copyright book, doing real argumentative work, in an entry that cites the book nowhere. Two separate assertions are made — that Galileo Was Wrong is the source of the film's CMB material, and that the book hedges harder than what descends from it — and neither carries a locator, a quotation, or a source-list entry. The same claim is repeated in the straw_man block ("Sungenis and Bennett's book is likewise more hedged than the list items derived from it, the same pattern already documented for their Michelson-Gale material"), where "already documented" points at a different argument's work, not at any evidence gathered here. This is the provenance-chain integrity check failing in our own showcase entry: claim X derives from source Y, asserted without a citation. It is also, in effect, a characterisation of two living authors' rhetorical care with nothing behind it — favourable to them, but still unsourced. And the hedge rule's second clause makes it worse: naming a hedge is precisely the finding we are obliged to demonstrate and publish, not to assert in passing.
holes.recommendation: Replace with: "Sungenis and Bennett's Galileo Was Wrong (7th ed., 2013) is the film's most likely textual source for the CMB material — Vol. II ch. 10 is the CMB chapter, and the same volume carries the authors' numbered “Claims and Responses” on the dipole. We have not yet held this cluster's items against those pages, so we make no claim here about how the book phrases the axis argument; the comparison is recorded as outstanding in the compression block below." Add to sources: {label: "Galileo Was Wrong, archive scan labelled …Bennett4276 — confirmed Volume II, 7th ed. 2013, chs 7-13; the CMB chapter is ch. 10", url: "https://archive.org/stream/GalileoWasWrongTheChurchSungenisRobertA.Bennett4276/Galileo%20Was%20Wrong_%20The%20Church%20%20-%20Sungenis,%20Robert%20A.%20&%20Bennett,_4276_djvu.txt"}.

holes.quoted_phrase: found three octopole planes orthogonal to the ecliptic
holes.description: Misreads the abstract we are quoting from in the same sentence. Schwarz et al. (PRL 93:221301, 2004), verified verbatim: "The quadrupole plane and the three octopole planes are remarkably aligned. Three of these planes are orthogonal to the ecliptic at a level inconsistent with gaussian random statistically isotropic skies at 99.8% C.L. … The remaining octopole plane is orthogonal to the supergalactic plane at >99.9% C.L." "These planes" is the set of four — one quadrupole plane plus three octopole planes — so the three orthogonal to the ecliptic include the quadrupole plane, and the fourth plane, which is an octopole plane, goes with the supergalactic plane instead. We have converted "three of four planes, one of them the quadrupole's" into "three octopole planes". The quoted C.L. is correct and the substance of our argument is untouched, but this is a defender's free win in a paragraph we introduce as "the point that matters most", and it is the same error class already logged twice in corrections.json: attributing to a source a claim adjacent to but not identical with what it says.
holes.recommendation: Replace with: "Schwarz et al. (2004) found the quadrupole plane and the three octopole planes remarkably aligned, with three of the four orthogonal to the ecliptic"

holes.quoted_phrase: aligned with the Galactic pole at 0.8–1.6%
holes.description: States the geometry backwards relative to the paper and to the rest of our own entry. Schwarz, Copi, Huterer & Starkman (CQG 33:184001, 2016), §2.2, verified from the arXiv PDF: the quadrupole-octopole plane is jointly perpendicular to the ecliptic plane at p = 2-4%, perpendicular to the Galactic pole at p = 0.8-1.6%, and aligned with the dipole direction at p = 0.09-0.37% (tightening to 0.06-0.23% after proper kinematic correction — which confirms our separate claim that correct removal of the kinematic quadrupole makes the alignments worse). Perpendicular to the Galactic POLE means lying in the Galactic PLANE, which is the opposite of "aligned with the Galactic pole". Our own surrounding text has it right twice — the TLDR says "the Galactic plane", and the sentence three lines above says "the plane of our galaxy" — so the entry contradicts itself in a list of quantitative results.
holes.recommendation: Replace with: "perpendicular to the Galactic pole at 0.8–1.6%"

holes.quoted_phrase: Its producer: the film “is not about geocentrism per se
holes.description: A direct quotation from a living person, used to characterise his position as inconsistent, with no citation anywhere in the entry and with a presentation that implies the wrong provenance. The quote is real — I verified it as part of DeLano's statement of 9 April 2014 — but our source_wording field runs it on immediately after the press-release material ("framed by the same release as a question… Its producer: the film…"), which reads as though it came from the press release. It did not: I fetched the release and it contains no attributed statement from DeLano at all. E01's twelve sources contain no link to the statement. The note then draws a conclusion about him — "so the scoping is not consistent" — which is a characterisation of a living person's rhetorical consistency resting on an uncited quote, and a further paraphrase, "he has elsewhere called geocentrism a profoundly important part of the story", which is not his wording; what he actually wrote in the same statement is that "any film about the Copernican Principle that does not involve an examination of geocentrism is a fatally flawed film". The characterisation survives on his own words, but only once those words are quoted accurately and cited. Under the harness this escalates rather than auto-patches.
holes.recommendation: Replace the run-on with a separately attributed sentence: "Separately, in a statement of 9 April 2014, producer Rick DeLano wrote that “The Principle”, as the title indicates, is not about geocentrism per se, but is instead an in-depth cinematic examination of the Copernican Principle itself — while adding, in the same statement, that any film about the Copernican Principle that does not involve an examination of geocentrism is a fatally flawed film. The two sentences scope the film narrowly and widely in turn; the list items keep only the wide reading." Add to sources: {label: "Rick DeLano, statement on The Principle and geocentrism, 9 April 2014", url: "https://magisterialfundies.blogspot.com/2014/04/statement-of-producer-of-principle.html"}.

holes.quoted_phrase: people=["PER-SUNGENIS"],
holes.description: The DEEP `people` list names only Sungenis, while the cluster record names "Robert Sungenis & Rick DeLano" as co-originators and the compression block quotes DeLano at length and draws a conclusion about him. A person we quote and characterise should be linked to his biography record, both so the reader can check what else we say about him and so the living-person review surface stays complete.
holes.recommendation: Replace with: people=["PER-SUNGENIS", "PER-DELANO"],  (add a PER-DELANO record in people.py if one does not exist; do not add the id without the record)

reviews.hedge_rule_note: PASSES, and this is the entry's strongest feature. The list fragments ("Preferred CMB dipole Earthward", "Dark flow directionality") are milder than the source, not stronger, and the refutation is aimed at the asserted original: DeLano's 10 July 2013 headline "CMB Dipole *Cannot Be Attributed to Earth's Motion*!!!" and the sentence he reproduces from the forthcoming edition ("an inherent microwave polarity in the composition of the Universe... physically divided in two along the Earth's equator"). I fetched that post and both are verbatim, with the "with permission"/"upcoming edition" framing our locator describes. The compression block also names the softening as a finding rather than using it as an escape hatch, which is the second clause of the rule. ONE caveat, short of the critical tier: the refutation repeatedly scores against a prediction of exactly zero from "an observer at rest at the centre of a spherically symmetric universe", which is a model the source explicitly amends in the same breath we quote (ether flow from Regulus; an intrinsic polarity). The entry does quote the amendment, so it is not refuting a fragment - but it re-uses the zero prediction afterwards as though the amendment had not been made (hole 3). The correct answer to the amended model is that it is unconstrained, not that it predicts zero.
reviews.summary: The physics is in unusually good shape - I re-verified the Planck 2018, Planck 2015 V, Planck 2013 XXVII, Planck Int. XIII, Atrio-Barandela, Kashlinsky, Watkins, Kothari, Secrest x3, Darling, Abghari, Wagenveld and Tomozawa citations against the sources, and independently recomputed every number in the refutation (3362.1 uK, 270.7 uK, 4.1 uK, RA 11h11.8m / Dec -6.94, ecliptic latitude 11.15 deg, 12%/19%, 5 Mpc) - all correct. The damage is in the provenance layer: the correction this entry logged in corrections.json as made to ARG-E03 was applied to ARG-E01 instead, so E03 still publishes the retracted "The Principle (film), 2014" attribution while the Method tab says it was withdrawn; the two works.py corrections the gloss announces were never made; the compression block's drifted=False makes the renderer print "Faithfully compressed" over a note saying the list states less than its source; and one paragraph attributes deliberate evasion ("insidiously coy") to living people, citing ARG-E01 for a characterisation ARG-E01 does not make.
citation_failures: MISMATCH - Singal, arXiv:1305.4134: our refutation says the anisotropies are 'ruled non-statistical at 99.995%'. The abstract (retrieved via ar5iv) gives the combined chance probability as ~2x10^-5, i.e. 99.998%. Our figure corresponds to 5x10^-5 and is not in the abstract.

MISMATCH - Singal, arXiv:1305.4134: we quote 'lie about a plane passing through the two equinoxes and the north celestial pole'. The paper reads 'The anisotropies lie about a plane passing through the equinoxes and the north celestial pole' - no 'two'. If the inserted word comes from the book's rendering of Singal, our sentence must say so.

TRIMMED QUOTE - Planck 2018 results I: our quote begins 'Photometric calibration from 30 to 353 GHz was based on the...'. The source sentence begins 'In the 2015 data release, photometric calibration from 30 to 353 GHz was based on...'. The scoping clause is dropped without an ellipsis.

UNVERIFIED (venue) - advocate field asserts Singal's 3CRR result is 'in Astronomy and Astrophysics'. I found no journal reference for arXiv:1305.4134; searches returned only preprint mirrors. Do not assert a venue we cannot show.

UNCHECKED (not failed) - every quotation from inside Galileo Was Wrong Vol. II ch. 10: Claim #12 ('If the Earth were the focal center...'), Claim #3 (COBE annual variation), Claim #5, the Regulus/'ether flow' answer, the 'Abuse of the Doppler effect' heading, the 18 uK standard deviation, and 'RA: 11hr 12mn, Decl: -7.06'. archive.org's fulltext-search endpoints returned 403/robots-disallowed and the djvu.txt truncates long before p. 371 under WebFetch. What I DID verify from the scan's front matter and contents: 'Seventh edition', 'Volume II, Chapters 7 to 13', and 'CMB Dipole Evidence: Claims and Responses - 371' inside ch. 10 Part 3, with Nodland-Ralston at 380 - so the ch. 10 / pp. 371-379 locator is sound.

UNCHECKED - Kothari et al. arXiv:1307.1947 v1 submission date (we say 8 July 2013, 'two days before the blog post'). arXiv's API is robots-blocked and the /abs page returns no metadata through WebFetch. Note also that the paper was retitled: it is now 'Dipole anisotropy in sky brightness and source count distribution in radio NVSS data' (Astropart. Phys.), so our source label cites a title only v1 bears - add 'v1'.

VERIFIED - Planck 2018 I (369.82 +/- 0.11 km/s, beta = 1.23357e-3, Local Group 620 +/- 15, 2015 nominal dipole subtracted); Planck 2015 V (270 uK orbital dipole, verbatim); Planck 2013 XXVII (384 +/- 78 stat +/- 115 syst, l,b = 264,48); Planck Int. XIII (no detection in any comoving sphere, 254 km/s 95% CL); Atrio-Barandela A&A 557:A116 (rotation inflates errors, simulations high by ~12%, significance returns to ~99%, 600-1000 km/s); Kashlinsky 2008 ('>300 h^-1 Mpc') and 2012 ('~800 Mpc'); Watkins 2023 (<0.03% at 150, <0.003% at 200 h^-1 Mpc); Kothari (1110 +/- 370 km/s; 'the Universe is intrinsically anisotropic...'); Secrest 2021 (ApJL 908:L51, 'over twice as large as expected', p=5e-7, 4.9 sigma, 1.36M quasars); Secrest 2022 (ApJL 937:L31, 5.1 sigma); RMP 97:041001 2025 ('exceeds 5 sigma in significance', 'a serious challenge to FLRW cosmology'); Darling 2022 (331 +161/-107, 399 +264/-199, 'consistent with the CMB dipole in direction and velocity'); Abghari 2024 ('consistent with a kinematic origin... within LambdaCDM', shot noise and clustering); Wagenveld et al. A&A 697:A112 2025 (39 +/- 8 deg offset; 5.4 sigma is in Sect. 4.2, not the abstract); Tomozawa arXiv:1108.1148 ('every body observes a cmb dipole which is equal to its Hubble flow velocity'); DeLano 10 July 2013 post (headline and 'inherent microwave polarity' sentence verbatim, 'with permission', cites arXiv:1307.1947v1); DeLano 18 May 2013 'Darkness and Evil in Cosmology' (four-item Axis of Evil list, third item 'Preferred direction of so-called dark flow').

holes.quoted_phrase: originator_work="The Principle (film)", year="2014"
holes.description: The correction this entry generated was logged as made and applied to the wrong cluster. review/corrections.json entry 13 says: where = 'scripts/clusters.py ARG-E03 - originator_work', old = 'Credited to The Principle (film), 2014.' But clusters.py line 445 (ARG-E03) still reads originator="Robert Sungenis & Rick DeLano", originator_work="The Principle (film)", year="2014" - and the correction comment, verbatim down to 'item 327 traces to DeLano's blog, 18 May 2013', was pasted into the ARG-E01 record instead (clusters.py lines 444-448 vs the E01 block above it), where item 327 does not live. data/flat-earth-origins-provenance.csv therefore publishes 'The Principle (film) / 2014' on all seven E03 rows (137, 294, 324, 327, 333, 343, 359) while the Method tab publishes the retraction of exactly that attribution. This is the single most discrediting defect available to a critic of a site whose product is provenance and whose credibility mechanism is its own corrections log: the log and the data contradict each other, and the fix was applied to a neighbouring cluster.
holes.recommendation:
Replace the ARG-E03 head in scripts/clusters.py with:
"E03": dict(lane="E", name="CMB dipole, dark flow and bulk-flow directionality",
    # Corrected 2026-08-08: the dipole argument is TEXTUAL, not filmic. It runs to
