    # "dark flow" and "bulk flow" occur ZERO times in all three volumes - item 327
    # traces to DeLano's blog, 18 May 2013, not to the book or the film.
    originator="Robert Sungenis & Rick DeLano",
    originator_work="Galileo Was Wrong (7th ed., 2013), Vol. I ch. 3 and Vol. II ch. 10",
    year="2013",
Then delete the item-327 sentence from the comment block on ARG-E01, which describes E03's evidence, and append a second corrections.json entry: {"at": "2026-08-09", "found_by": "curmudgeon, ARG-E03 cycle 1", "where": "scripts/clusters.py - ARG-E03 and ARG-E01", "old_argument": "Corrections entry 13 recorded the E03 originator_work as corrected from 'The Principle (film)', 2014.", "new_argument": "The edit was applied to ARG-E01 and not to ARG-E03; E03 continued to publish the retracted attribution across seven dataset rows until 2026-08-09.", "reason": "A correction logged as made and not made is worse than an uncorrected error, because the log is what readers are asked to trust."}

holes.quoted_phrase: assessed=True, drifted=False
holes.description: drifted=False makes render.py emit the summary line 'Faithfully compressed' with the standfirst 'The one-line item states this claim at the strength its source states it' (scripts/render.py, the `elif cp["assessed"] is True` branch, lines ~173-181). The note inside that collapsed block says the opposite in its first sentence: 'The list is not stronger than its source here. It is weaker, and that is the finding... On six of the seven items the compressed phrasing states less than the original, and in two cases much less.' A reader who does not expand sees the false claim; a reader who does expand sees us contradict our own headline. deep.py defines drift_type='none' as 'the list states the source's claim at the source's strength', which by the entry's own evidence is not what happened. The seven-value enum has no slot for softening - curmudgeon.md says to name that in the review rather than force it into the nearest box, and forcing it into 'none' is what happened here.
holes.recommendation:
Add an optional headline pair to the compression dict in scripts/_b7_E03.py, immediately after drift_type="none": headline="The list understates its own source", headline_tldr="The one-line items claim less than the book and the blog do. We answer the original, and we publish the gap - the fragment a reader arrives with is milder than the proclamation it descends from.", and in scripts/render.py replace the two literals in the not-drifted branch with: f'{cp.get("headline", "Faithfully compressed")}' f'

{cp.get("headline_tldr", "The one-line item states this claim at the strength its source states it — so the original is what we answer, and the original is what the list has.")}

' Leave drifted=False (nothing was hardened) and add to deep.py's drift_type documentation: "The enum records hardening only. Where the list SOFTENS its source, keep drifted=False and say so in `note` and `headline` - the gap is still a finding."

holes.quoted_phrase: Being wrong by a factor of two is a better position than being wrong by infinity
holes.description: The zero prediction is applied to a model the source has already amended, in the same entry that quotes the amendment. Our own refutation reports the book's answer to its Claim #12 - the dipole is ether flow from the Regulus direction, or 'an inherent microwave polarity in the composition of the Universe'. A model with an intrinsic microwave polarity and an ether flow predicts a nonzero dipole and gives no reason to expect a source-count dipole of zero either; the number-count anomaly's own authors describe it as an intrinsic anisotropy of the matter distribution, which is nearer the source's amended position than to ours. So 'wrong by infinity' scores against a spherically symmetric geostatic model that the source explicitly abandons two paragraphs earlier, and a well-informed defender goes for this first - it is the only place in a careful entry where we hit a position nobody in the cluster holds. The same move recurs in the closing paragraph ('and which the geocentric model predicts should not exist') and in the steelman's 'predicts a source-count dipole of zero and a CMB dipole of zero'. The honest answer is not that the amended model predicts zero, but that it predicts nothing: an intrinsic polarity of unspecified size, direction and spectrum accommodates a dipole twice our velocity exactly as comfortably as one matching it, and a model that fits any amplitude is not confirmed by the one observed.
holes.recommendation: Replace the sentence with: "The geocentric model in its unamended form predicts zero, which is why the source amends it — and the amendment is the problem. An intrinsic microwave polarity of unspecified amplitude, direction and spectrum accommodates a matter dipole twice our velocity exactly as comfortably as one matching it, or half it, or none at all. A model that fits every possible value of the anomaly is not supported by the value observed; the kinematic model, by contrast, predicted the direction, and the excess is measured against that prediction rather than against nothing." Then change the closing paragraph's "and which the geocentric model predicts should not exist" to "and which the geocentric model predicts only once it has been amended to predict anything at all", and the steelman's "a stationary Earth at the centre of a spherically symmetric universe predicts a source-count dipole of zero and a CMB dipole of zero" to "a stationary Earth at the centre of a spherically symmetric universe predicts both dipoles to be zero — which is why the source replaces the symmetry with an intrinsic polarity, and why the amended model constrains nothing".

holes.quoted_phrase: promotional register is insidiously coy
holes.description: An imputation of deliberate deception to living people, sourced to a sibling entry that does not make it. 'Insidiously coy' says the film's producers chose evasive wording in order to entrap or mislead - a motive claim about Rick DeLano and Robert Sungenis, both living, which the project's standing constraint puts off limits unless directly sourced. It is also a misquotation of our own record: ARG-E01 (scripts/deep_batch4.py) says only that the film 'does not claim the Sun orbits a stationary Earth', that its framing is 'narrower and more defensible-sounding', and that Galileo Was Wrong 'is more hedged than the claims descending from it'. Nothing in E01 characterises intent. The same escalation appears in the gloss: 'ARG-E01 records that The Principle's promotional wording is careful to the point of evasion' - 'careful to the point of evasion' is likewise ours, not E01's. The observation underneath is sound and sourced; only the adjectives are unsupported, which makes this a cheap fix and an expensive thing to leave in on a page that criticises others for attributing more than their sources say.
holes.recommendation: Replace with: "The standing warning about this originator — recorded at ARG-E01 — is that The Principle's promotional register is markedly more hedged than the list, saying patterns seem to align rather than asserting, so that a rebuttal aimed at the list's flat phrasing beats a straw man." And in the gloss, replace "ARG-E01 records that The Principle's promotional wording is careful to the point of evasion" with "ARG-E01 records that The Principle's promotional wording is notably more guarded than the claims descending from it".

holes.quoted_phrase: Two further corrections to works.py follow from that page
holes.description: The corrections were announced and never made, and the record they were meant to fix is rendered. scripts/works.py WRK-SUNGENIS-2006 still carries imprint="With Robert J. Bennett. Vol. I, The Scientific Case for Geocentrism, 2006; Vol. II historical; Vol. III church history. 10th ed. 2013." - and render.py line 287 prints the imprint verbatim on the Works tab. So the site tells one reader that Volume II is the historical volume and that the 2013 printing is the tenth edition, while ARG-E03 tells the next reader that Volume II is chapters 7-13 of the scientific argument and that the 2013 printing is the seventh. I confirmed E03's version directly from the archive scan's front matter and contents page: 'Seventh edition', 'Volume II, Chapters 7 to 13', ch. 10 'Technical and Summary Analysis of Geocentrism' running to 'CMB Dipole Evidence: Claims and Responses - 371'. Under the harness a wrong edition is major on its own; a wrong edition that our own entry has already identified in print, and that no corrections.json entry records, is worse. Note this is the same failure mode as hole 1 - batch 7 wrote up two record corrections and applied neither.
holes.recommendation: Replace the imprint in scripts/works.py with: imprint="With Robert J. Bennett. First published 2006 as Vol. I, The Scientific Case for Geocentrism. Seventh edition, Catholic Apologetics International Publishing, 2013, in three volumes: Vol. I chs 1-6 and Vol. II chs 7-13, both the scientific argument, and Vol. III chs 14-17, church history and theology. The five previous editions, in two volumes, ran 2005-2010." and append to review/corrections.json: {"at": "2026-08-09", "found_by": "curmudgeon, ARG-E03 cycle 1", "where": "scripts/works.py WRK-SUNGENIS-2006 - imprint", "old_argument": "Vol. II historical; Vol. III church history. 10th ed. 2013.", "new_argument": "The seventh edition's own front matter divides the work Vol. I chs 1-6, Vol. II chs 7-13 (both scientific), Vol. III chs 14-17 (church history); the 2013 printing is the seventh edition, not the tenth.", "reason": "Identified in ARG-E03's gloss on 2026-08-08 and left unapplied for a day; the Works tab contradicted the argument page in the meantime."}

holes.quoted_phrase: it is our own velocity written across the sky
holes.description: The TLDR states as settled the one thing the entry elsewhere refuses to state as settled. The body concedes that the boosting measurement's 'error bars are wide enough that an intrinsic contribution of order 100 km/s is not excluded by this test alone', the straw_man field warns in our own voice against writing 'as though the whole subject were closed', and the file docstring makes E01's restraint rule binding here. The RMP 2025 Colloquium I verified puts the matter dipole excess above 5 sigma and says it demonstrates 'either the rest frames in which matter and radiation appear isotropic are not the same, or that there is an unexpected intrinsic anisotropy in at least one of them' - the second disjunct is a live possibility that the CMB dipole is not wholly kinematic. Readers see the TLDR first and many never expand, so the one place the entry overstates is the place it costs most.
holes.recommendation: Replace with: "it is, to the precision anyone has measured it, our own velocity written across the sky"

holes.quoted_phrase: recomputed here, and equal to the measured amplitude to four figures
holes.description: This is a definition dressed as a confirmation, and it is the first quantitative move in the refutation. Planck derives v = 369.82 km/s from the measured amplitude 3362.08 uK by dividing by T_0 - so recomputing beta*T_0 from that velocity and finding 3362.1 uK cannot test anything; it recovers the input. I ran it: 1.23357e-3 x 2.7255 K = 3362.095 uK, which is arithmetic on Planck's own quoted beta, not a check of it. The framing 'worth doing rather than trusting' invites the reader to treat it as verification, and the closing paragraph then lists it first among four pillars of the verdict: 'a signal whose amplitude matches our velocity to four significant figures'. A defender who spots this gets to say the page does not understand which of its own numbers are independent - unnecessarily, since the orbital modulation and the Doppler-boosting measurement are genuinely independent and do the work.
holes.recommendation: Replace with: "recomputed here, and identical to the measured amplitude, because the two are the same statement: Planck's quoted velocity is that amplitude divided by T0. Nothing is confirmed by the arithmetic; what it fixes is the exchange rate, so that the independent tests below can be read as velocities." And in the closing paragraph, replace "a signal whose amplitude matches our velocity to four significant figures, whose annual variation" with "a signal whose annual variation".

holes.quoted_phrase: “Photometric calibration from 30 to 353 GHz was based on the ‘orbital dipole’, i.e., the modulation of the Solar dipole induced by the orbital motion of the satellite around the Solar System barycentre.”
holes.description: We trim a scoping clause out of a quotation without an ellipsis, in the paragraph we call the clincher. Planck 2018 results I reads 'In the 2015 data release, photometric calibration from 30 to 353 GHz was based on the "orbital dipole"...' - I retrieved the sentence from the A&A full text. Our version silently promotes a statement about the 2015 release into an unscoped present-tense claim, which we then reinforce with 'Planck does not merely detect it. It calibrates on it.' The substance survives (the 2018 release also calibrates on the orbital dipole), so this is not a false claim - but it is precisely the compression manoeuvre this project exists to document, performed by us, on the load-bearing quotation of the entry.
holes.recommendation: Replace with: "“In the 2015 data release, photometric calibration from 30 to 353 GHz was based on the ‘orbital dipole’, i.e., the modulation of the Solar dipole induced by the orbital motion of the satellite around the Solar System barycentre” — and the 2018 release calibrates the same way."

holes.quoted_phrase: That is roughly 3–3.5σ,
holes.description: We shave the other side's strongest recent number. Watkins et al. (2023) report - I checked the abstract - less than a 0.03% chance at 150 h^-1 Mpc and less than 0.003% at 200 h^-1 Mpc, which the paper deliberately states as probabilities rather than sigmas. Converted one-sided those are 3.4 and 4.0 sigma, not '3-3.5'. The steelman's job is to state the opposing case at full strength before answering it, and the entry's own advocate paragraph then repeats the understatement ('your standard model gets wrong at three sigma'). Since the refutation's reply to bulk flows does not depend on the size of the tension - a bulk flow is a peculiar velocity field either way - there is nothing to gain by rounding it down and a straightforward accusation of shaving to invite.
holes.recommendation: Replace with: "Converted one-sided those are about 3.4σ and 4.0σ — the paper states them as probabilities rather than sigmas, and they are recent, and they should be conceded without hedging."

holes.quoted_phrase: ruled non-statistical at 99.995%
holes.description: The figure is not the one in the paper. Singal (arXiv:1305.4134) gives the combined chance probability for the 3CRR asymmetries as ~2x10^-5, i.e. 99.998%; 99.995% corresponds to 5x10^-5 and appears nowhere in the abstract I retrieved. In the same sentence we quote Singal as writing 'lie about a plane passing through the two equinoxes and the north celestial pole' - the paper reads 'the equinoxes', with no 'two'. Both errors are conservative in our favour, which is how they survived, and both are checkable in one click by a defender who is already being told this page checks its quotations.
holes.recommendation: Replace the clause with: "anisotropies in the 3CRR quasar and radio-galaxy distribution that “lie about a plane passing through the equinoxes and the north celestial pole”, with a combined chance probability of ~2×10<sup>−5</sup>"

holes.quoted_phrase: Numbers recomputed in-session from the published velocities (2026-08-08); see the refutation.
holes.description: No regression test pins any of E03's recomputed numbers, against the repo's own stated house rule. tests/test_provenance.py opens with 'every numeric claim on the page must be derived from the dataset, and every derived number must be asserted here... Claims without tests rot', and it pins ARG-E01's careful-case language explicitly (lines 273-295). E03 introduces at least seven recomputed figures that carry the REFUTED verdict - 3362.1 uK, 271 uK, 4.1 uK, RA 11h11.8m / Dec -6.94 deg, 11.2 deg from the ecliptic, 12% and 19%, 5 Mpc - and none is asserted anywhere. I reproduced all of them and they are right today; the rule exists because nobody will re-derive them after the next edit.
holes.recommendation:
Add to tests/test_provenance.py, after the E01 block:
print("\n[9] E03 recomputed numbers")
import math
_c, _T0 = 299792.458, 2.7255
check("E03 dipole amplitude follows from the Planck velocity",
      abs(369.82/_c*_T0*1e6 - 3362.1) < 0.2)
check("E03 orbital dipole follows from Earth's orbital speed",
      abs(29.78/_c*_T0*1e6 - 271) < 1.0)
check("E03 kinematic quadrupole follows from beta squared",
      abs((369.82/_c)**2*_T0*1e6 - 4.1) < 0.2)
_e03 = ARGS["ARG-E03"]["refutation"]
for _s in ("3362.1", "271 µK", "11.8", "6.94", "11.2", "5 Mpc"):
    check(f"E03 still carries the recomputed figure {_s}", _s in _e03)

holes.quoted_phrase: the same measurement with the Sun's galactic orbit and the Galaxy's motion within the Local Group added back
holes.description: Wrong direction. The Local Group velocity is obtained by removing the Sun's orbit about the Galactic centre and the Galaxy's motion within the Local Group from the solar-dipole velocity, not by adding them back: v_LG = v_Sun(CMB) - v_Sun(LG). The point being made - that the two figures are one measurement plus known local corrections, not two independent results - is correct and worth keeping.
holes.recommendation: Replace with "the same measurement with the Sun's galactic orbit and the Galaxy's motion within the Local Group taken out"

holes.quoted_phrase: matching the Earth's orbital speed to within a microkelvin
holes.description: Overstated precision, in the sentence that carries the verdict. This is in the verdict_challenge reasoning (the field enum has no slot for it, so it is filed under refutation). Planck's '270 uK' is a rounded parenthetical quoted to two significant figures, not a measurement with sub-microkelvin precision; our computed value is 270.74 uK. A match cannot be claimed tighter than the figure it is matched against. Nothing rests on the tightness - agreement to the quoted precision, in the right plane and phase, already defeats the assimilation move the paragraph is answering.
holes.recommendation: Replace with "matching the Earth's orbital speed to the precision Planck states it"

holes.quoted_phrase: “The kinematic contribution to the cosmic number count dipole”, A&A (2025)
holes.description: Two source labels are thinner than the rest of a meticulous list. The 2025 A&A paper is unattributed and unpaginated: it is Wagenveld, von Hausegger, Kloeckner & Schwarz, A&A 697:A112 (2025), and the 5.4 sigma figure we cite is in Sect. 4.2 rather than the abstract, which is worth saying since a checker who reads only the abstract will not find it. The Kothari label cites the v1 title; the paper was retitled 'Dipole anisotropy in sky brightness and source count distribution in radio NVSS data' on publication, so a reader following the arXiv link finds a different title from ours.
holes.recommendation: Replace the label with: "Wagenveld, von Hausegger, Kloeckner & Schwarz, “The kinematic contribution to the cosmic number count dipole”, A&A 697:A112 (2025) — residual non-kinematic dipole at 5.4σ (Sect. 4.2), offset 39 ± 8° from the CMB dipole" and amend the Kothari label to "... (arXiv:1307.1947v1, July 2013; published, retitled, as ‘Dipole anisotropy in sky brightness and source count distribution in radio NVSS data’) — the version DeLano cites two days after it appeared".

holes.quoted_phrase: his words, in Astronomy and Astrophysics, not mine
holes.description: An unverifiable venue put in the mouth of our own advocate. I could find no journal reference for Singal's 3CRR paper (arXiv:1305.4134); searches return preprint mirrors only. The advocate block is not rendered, so reader impact is nil, but a claim we cannot support should not sit in our files even in a role-played voice - and if the entry is ever mined for the body text, the false venue travels with it.
holes.recommendation: Replace with "his words, in his own paper, not mine"

reviews.hedge_rule_note: The rule is satisfied, and E13 is one of the better applications of it on the page. Where a source exists the refutation answers the source, not the fragment: item 334 is answered by taking Celerier's actual disjunction (verified verbatim against A&A 353:63 / astro-ph/9907206 - "does not exclude the possibility of ruling out the Cosmological Principle - and cosmological constant - hypotheses" and "either a strictly positive cosmological constant in an homogeneous universe or large scale inhomogeneity with no constraint on Lambda") and then refuting the LTB void programme on measurement; item 358 is answered by taking Nodland and Ralston's own hedge ("Barring hidden systematic bias in the data, the correlation indicates a new cosmological effect." - verified in the PRL abstract) plus the three 1997 rebuttals. The compression block also honours the second clause: it publishes the gap as a finding rather than retreating to "nobody really claims this", and it says out loud that the drift_type enum is a loose fit because a bare topic label cannot drop a hedge by itself - the assertion is supplied by the frame. That analysis is right and should not be forced into the enum. One residual exposure, filed as a hole rather than a rule breach: the refutation says Vol. II "presents it as standing" against those rebuttals, but the Vol. II contents line is "Nodland-Ralston Evidence: Claims and Responses 380", the authors' own objection-and-reply format. If those replies engage Wardle, Carroll or Eisenstein, our section 4 answers the 1997 paper instead of the book's defence of it - the hedge rule's failure mode moved one link up the chain.
citation_failures: FAILED - sources[] label for Sungenis 2011, NPA Proceedings: '(searched; contains none of these six topics)'. The PDF at the URL we ourselves cite does contain the item-334 topic: it quotes Clifton ('Studies of Type Ia supernovae, together with the Copernican principle, have led to the inference that the Universe is accelerating in its expansion'; 'Alternatively, it could be the case that the Copernican Principle is invalid, and that the data has been interpreted within an inappropriate theoretical framework'; 'If we were to live in a special place in the Universe, near the centre of a void where the local matter density is low, then the supernovae observations would be accounted for without the addition of dark energy'), quotes Ellis on large-scale inhomogeneity, and describes a void with the Earth at or near its centre. The negative claim is false and the paper is a second ancestor for item 334.

UNRESOLVED - gloss, item 194: the quotation attributed to 'Urban and Zhitnitsky' is not corroborated. Their paper on this subject, 'Cosmological constant, violation of cosmological isotropy and CMB' (arXiv:0906.3546, JCAP 2009/09/018), contains no occurrence of 'polarisation' or 'polarization' in its full text. Either the book quotes a different Urban and Zhitnitsky paper, which we should name, or the attribution inside the book is wrong and we are passing it on unmarked.

UNCHECKED (access, not accuracy) - Galileo Was Wrong Vol. II pp. 380-383, the quoted birefringence passage; Vol. I p. 252 n., the supernova footnote; Vol. I pp. 413-415, the Urban and Zhitnitsky quotation. The archive.org djvu.txt for both the three-volume item and the Vol. II item (Bennett4276, 1.7 MB) truncates long before those pages on every route tried, and the archive full-text search endpoints are robots-disallowed. Confirmed from the Vol. II front matter: the contents line 'Nodland-Ralston Evidence: Claims and Responses 380', which corroborates volume, chapter and page of the locator.

VERIFIED - Celerier 2000 (both quoted phrases exact); Zumalacarregui et al. 2012 (Omega_in>0.2 vs <0.15, 3 sigma apart, 'ruled out at high confidence'); Moss, Zibin & Scott 2011 (all eight observables, low local Hubble rate, old-age problem, too little local structure); Caldwell & Stebbins 2008 ('the largest voids which mimic cosmic acceleration'); Zhang & Stebbins 2011 (ACT and SPT kSZ limits, adiabatic void); Blomqvist & Mortsell 2010 (fifteen per cent from supernovae alone, about one per cent with the CMB dipole); Eisenstein et al. 2005 (46,748 LRGs, 100 h^-1 Mpc, 5 per cent to z=0.35); DESI DR2 (>14 million objects, 2.3 sigma, PRD 112:083515); DESI 2024 IV (420,000 forest spectra, 700,000 quasars, H(2.33)=(239.2+/-4.8)(147.09/r_d)); Nodland & Ralston 1997; Wardle, Perley & Cohen 1997 ('A least squares fit to the radio data has a slope only 2% of their claimed effect'); Minami & Komatsu 2020 (0.35+/-0.14 deg); Eskilt & Komatsu 2022 (0.342 +0.094/-0.091, 3.6 sigma, 23-353 GHz); Diego-Palazuelos et al. 2022 (quote exact, beta falls as the mask grows); SPT-3G 2025 (1.2e-4, 0.53e-4 with lensing prior); Webb et al. 2011 (4.2 sigma, RA 17.5+/-0.9 h, dec -58+/-9 deg); Whitmore & Murphy 2015; Murphy et al. 2022 (1.3+/-1.3+/-0.4 ppm, laser frequency comb); Stiskalek, Desmond & Lavaux (MNRAS 546(2) staf2048, published 22 January 2026 - our '2026' is right; 0.087+/-0.019 mag, 4.1+/-0.9 per cent, 877:1, 0.049+/-0.013 mag Pantheon+, bulk flow 'fully consistent with expectations from the standard cosmological model'); the specimen list (heading '435 Pieces of Evidence The Earth is Not A Spinning Ball' and banner '461 REASONS I DO NOT BELIEVE THE EARTH IS A SPINNING BALL' both present, difference 26 as claimed; items 194 and 330-359 verbatim as in our corpus; item 194 four lines from 'Earth heart chakra symbolism'); and the internal arithmetic (29 clusters now carry originator=None, so 30 before this correction and 28 unaudited; 372 traced items and 134 Sungenis items, matching corrections.json).
reviews.summary: E13 is a strong entry: the steelman is at kernel tier, the physics citations are unusually accurate - I checked twenty of them against the papers, including every number in the void, BAO, Lyman-alpha, birefringence and Tully-Fisher sections, and found no error in any - and the compression block is the most honest on the page about the limits of its own enum. The damage is elsewhere. Section 7 asserts a distance floor that section 5 breaks, because the Tully-Fisher and Pantheon+ samples we rely on are restricted to z<0.05; a source label tells the reader the Sungenis 2011 NPA paper contains none of the six topics when it carries the supernova-void alternative at length; the refutation's closing clause states as fact a claim about how the list was assembled that the gloss expressly disclaims two paragraphs earlier, about a named living compiler; and the TLDR counts two traced items where the record says three and credits the Lyman-alpha forest with breaking the void model, which the body never claims. The verdict NOT DEMONSTRATED holds and the hedge rule is satisfied.

holes.quoted_phrase: every measurement here is of objects between 300 Mpc and the surface of last scattering
holes.short_summary: Section 7 contradicts section 5 on distances
holes.description: The closing sweep asserts a distance floor our own section 5 breaks. Stiskalek, Desmond and Lavaux (MNRAS 546(2), staf2048, 22 January 2026), which section 5 relies on and concedes in full, restricts every sample to z<0.05 - CosmicFlows-4 Tully-Fisher W1 at z_CMB<~0.05, 2MTF at z_CMB<~0.03, SFI++ at z_CMB<~0.05, Pantheon+ at z_CMB<=0.05. That is roughly 200 Mpc and less. So the one item in the cluster where we concede a real directional detection is a measurement of objects entirely inside the radius we have just told the reader nothing here goes inside, and a defender answers our summary paragraph with our own strongest concession.
holes.recommendation: Ask what any of this would distinguish. Not one item separates a flat, stationary Earth from an ordinary spinning globe. The objects run from spiral galaxies a few tens of Mpc away, in the Tully–Fisher samples, out to the surface of last scattering, and every measurement of them is equally available on either account.

holes.quoted_phrase: searched; contains none of these six topics
holes.short_summary: NPA paper label states a false negative
holes.description: We tell the reader that Sungenis's 2011 NPA paper contains none of the six topics. It contains the item-334 topic at length: it quotes Clifton - 'Studies of Type Ia supernovae, together with the Copernican principle, have led to the inference that the Universe is accelerating in its expansion' and 'If we were to live in a special place in the Universe, near the centre of a void where the local matter density is low, then the supernovae observations would be accounted for without the addition of dark energy' - quotes Ellis on large-scale inhomogeneity, and describes a void with the Earth at or near its centre. A defender needs only to open the PDF at the URL in our own sources list. On a page whose product is provenance, in the entry whose headline finding is that our 'untraced' label failed an audit, a false negative in the search log is the most expensive error available - and the correction runs our way, since the paper is a second ancestor for item 334.
holes.recommendation: Sungenis 2011, NPA Proceedings — 'Cosmological Evidence Shows Central and Non-Moving Earth' (searched: no BAO, Tully–Fisher, Lyman-alpha or birefringence material, but it does carry the supernova-dimming alternative, quoting Clifton — 'If we were to live in a special place in the Universe, near the centre of a void where the local matter density is low, then the supernovae observations would be accounted for without the addition of dark energy' — and Ellis on large-scale inhomogeneity, so item 334 has an ancestor here as well as in Vol. I)

holes.quoted_phrase: which is what happens when a vocabulary is swept rather than an argument followed
holes.short_summary: Asserts as fact what the gloss says we cannot show
holes.description: The refutation's final clause states as established fact a claim about how the list was produced. The gloss, two paragraphs earlier, says of exactly this claim: 'Whatever produced the block, it was sweeping a technical vocabulary rather than following a source. We cannot show that, and we do not assert it.' A critic putting the two side by side gets a self-contradiction inside one entry, and the version asserted without qualification is an unsupported claim about the working method of a named living compiler, which our own rules put in the escalate tier. The disclaimer makes it worse rather than better: it shows we knew the claim was unsupported when we published it in the body.
holes.recommendation: The list is carrying its own refutation as the adjacent entry. We do not know how the block was assembled and do not speculate about it; what can be said is narrower and enough — items 333 and 334 cannot both point the same way, because the kinetic Sunyaev–Zel'dovich measurement named in one is what excluded the void required by the other.

holes.quoted_phrase: nevertheless presents it as standing
holes.short_summary: Unverified claim that Vol. II ignores the 1997 rebuttals
holes.description: We characterise Vol. II as presenting the Nodland-Ralston result as standing, immediately after listing three rebuttals, without establishing whether the book answers them. The Vol. II contents page reads 'Nodland-Ralston Evidence: Claims and Responses 380' - the same 'Claims and Responses' structure our ARG-E03 record documents across Vol. I ch. 3 and Vol. II ch. 10, in which the authors state an objection and reply to it. If Eisenstein and Bunn, Carroll and Field, or Wardle, Perley and Cohen are among the claims answered there, a defender disposes of our whole section 4 in one sentence: the book replies to all three on the pages you cite, and you refuted the 1997 paper instead of the reply. I could not read the section body (see citation notes), which is precisely why the sentence should not assert what it asserts.
holes.recommendation: Volume II of Galileo Was Wrong nevertheless presents it as standing, adds that the axis lies on the equinox line, and concludes that the sources are “symmetric around AND centered on the Earth”. One thing we owe the reader here: that material sits under a heading, Nodland-Ralston Evidence: Claims and Responses, which is the authors' format for stating an objection and answering it, and we have not been able to read those answers in the scan available to us. We do not claim the 1997 rebuttals went unnoticed there. We claim only what the journal record shows: the result did not survive 1997 in the journal that published it.

holes.quoted_phrase: The other four name real measurements and stop
holes.short_summary: TLDR says two traced, the record says three
holes.description: The TLDR counts two traced items and asserts the other four merely name measurements and stop. The gloss says 'Three of the six items have a documented ancestor', the entry docstring says the same, and the cluster note says 'Three of six items trace to Sungenis & Bennett'. Readers meet the TLDR first and many never expand, so the version most of them leave with is the one that contradicts our own record, and it silently withdraws the item-194 finding without saying it is doing so.
holes.recommendation: Two of these six items descend from Sungenis and Bennett and a third probably does, which makes our own record — which filed this cluster as untraced — wrong. The rest name real measurements and stop, and one of them, BAO, is the standard ruler that broke the void model the supernova item needs. The one anisotropy in the cluster that is genuinely measured, a 4 per cent dipole in Tully–Fisher distances, is explained by our own motion.

holes.quoted_phrase: BAO and the Lyman-alpha forest, are the standard rulers that broke the void model
holes.short_summary: TLDR credits Lyman-alpha with killing the void model
holes.description: The TLDR tells the reader that BAO and the Lyman-alpha forest are the rulers that broke the void model. The body never claims this of the Lyman-alpha forest, and the papers we cite for the kill do not use it: Zumalacarregui, Garcia-Bellido and Ruiz-Lapuente (JCAP 2012) use galaxy and radial BAO, Moss, Zibin and Scott (PRD 2011) use radial BAO among eight observables, and the DESI Lyman-alpha measurement we cite is from 2024 and appears in the body only as a two per cent determination of H(z=2.33). A TLDR that attributes to our own evidence something our own evidence does not say is the overstatement pattern the harness singles out.
holes.recommendation: The rest name real measurements and stop, and one of them, BAO, is the standard ruler that broke the void model the supernova item needs.

holes.quoted_phrase: it is implicit in the word
holes.short_summary: Straw-man block contradicts the compression block
holes.description: The straw_man block locates a misrepresentation of cosmology inside the wording of a two-word item label, while the compression block argues in bold that 'these items are not assertions at all - they are topic labels, and a label cannot drop a hedge by itself. The assertion is supplied by the frame the labels sit in.' Both cannot hold: either a label can carry an assertion, and the compression analysis is wrong, or it cannot, and the straw man is not in the word 'alternatives'. The substance of the block - that the inhomogeneous alternative was proposed, developed and killed by cosmologists - is correct and verified, and only its location needs moving.
holes.recommendation: These items are labels, not assertions, so the straw man is not in their wording — it is in the frame that collects them. Standard cosmology is presented as though model-dependence were something cosmologists conceal and an outsider had noticed. The record is the reverse: the inhomogeneous alternative to dark energy was proposed by a cosmologist in Astronomy & Astrophysics, developed for a decade in Physical Review D and JCAP, and killed by cosmologists using BAO, the kSZ effect, the CMB spectrum and the local structure amplitude.

holes.quoted_phrase: Riess and 15 collaborators on 16 objects
holes.short_summary: Riess 1998 has 20 authors, not 16
holes.description: The author count is wrong. Riess et al. 1998, AJ 116:1009 carries twenty authors - Riess, Filippenko, Challis, Clocchiatti, Diercks, Garnavich, Gilliland, Hogan, Jha, Kirshner, Leibundgut, Phillips, Reiss, Schmidt, Schommer, Smith, Spyromilio, Stubbs, Suntzeff, Tonry - so it is Riess and nineteen collaborators. The paired Perlmutter figure (31 collaborators, 42 supernovae) is exactly right, which makes the miss conspicuous, and the point of stating collaborator counts at all was to show the result is not one person's.
holes.recommendation: Riess and 19 collaborators on 16 objects, Perlmutter and 31 collaborators on 42

Galileo Was Wrong Vol. I, ch. 1, p. 30 states that George F. R. Ellis proposed "a new model of cosmology... that proposed the Earth was in a central position in the universe", and its footnote 57 quotes Paul C. W. Davies: "...as we see only redshifts whichever direction we look in the sky, the only way in which this could be consistent with a gravitational explanation is if the Earth is situated at the center of an inhomogeneous Universe." That is this cluster's inference verbatim - same-in-every-direction therefore Earth-at-the-centre - with a named author (Ellis), a named publication (Davies in Nature), and a citation. Our own steelman and refutation then spend their strongest paragraphs killing exactly that model (the Lemaitre-Tolman-Bondi void), and our own ARG-E13 entry traces item 334 to Vol. I ch. 2's Celerier LTB footnote: the same book, the same argument, audited by us eight days later. The Hawking isotropy quote-mine ("all this evidence that the universe looks the same whichever direction we look might seem to suggest there is something special about our place in the universe") is also carried by the downstream geocentric quote compilations we claim to have covered. This is the same class of error already logged twice in corrections.json - entry 4 (R06, cluster-level attribution applied without checking each item) and entry 12 (E13, 'untraced' asserted at triage and never tested) - and E17 is the audit those entries cite as the one that was tested.

holes.quoted_phrase: Its rough uniformity around the sky is a fact about the atmosphere being a shell we sit at the bottom of.
holes.description: Factually wrong, and it concedes a premise we did not have to concede. Scintillation is strongly anisotropic in zenith angle: the amplitude rises steeply toward the horizon with the length of the air column (weak-turbulence theory gives roughly a sec(z) to the 11/6 scaling), which is why stars near the horizon visibly boil while a star at zenith is nearly steady, and it varies further with the high-altitude wind. What is approximately symmetric is the azimuthal distribution about the observer's vertical, not the distribution 'around the sky'. As written we grant the item's premise for scintillation while denying the identical premise for item 9 two paragraphs later - inconsistent inside one entry, and a defender will find it.
holes.recommendation: Replace with: "It is not in fact uniform around the sky: the amplitude climbs steeply toward the horizon, where the light traverses a far longer column of air, which is why low stars visibly boil while a star overhead is nearly steady. What is roughly symmetric is the distribution in azimuth about the observer's own vertical — a fact about standing at the bottom of a spherical shell of air, and about that observer rather than about the Earth."

holes.quoted_phrase: That is a genuine model — the Lemaître–Tolman–Bondi void — and it was taken seriously enough in the 2000s to be proposed as an alternative to dark energy.
holes.description: Right but rhetorically exposed, and it is the first thing a well-informed defender reaches for. The single most-circulated sentence supporting this exact cluster is Ellis's own - "I can construct you a spherically symmetrical universe with Earth at its centre, and you cannot disprove it based on observations... you can only exclude it on philosophical grounds" (Scientific American, October 1995) - and it is the passage Galileo Was Wrong builds on at Vol. I ch. 1 p. 30. Our steelman describes the model without naming the authority the argument's own literature cites for it, and the advocate block (survives=3) does not deploy it either. A reader who arrives with that quote will not find it answered here, and the answer we have is a good one: Ellis said it in 1995, and the observational disproof he said did not exist was published in 2011.
holes.recommendation: Append to that steelman paragraph: "And the geocentric literature does not have to invent this: it cites the physicist who built the model. Ellis told Scientific American in October 1995 that he could construct a spherically symmetric universe with the Earth at its centre and that it could not be disproved from observation, only excluded on philosophical grounds — and Galileo Was Wrong opens on exactly that point (Vol. I, ch. 1, p. 30). Taken at its date, the concession was correct." Then add to the refutation's closing section: "The concession has an expiry date, and it has passed. Ellis was right in 1995 that the central-observer model was observationally unreachable. It stopped being unreachable in 2008 and 2011, when the CMB blackbody spectrum and then the kinetic Sunyaev–Zel'dovich power measured by ACT and SPT gave it a signature it does not have. Quoting the 1995 sentence today is quoting a physicist's description of the state of the evidence thirteen years before the evidence arrived."

The line is also wrong on the merits — terms appearing in a chart are coordinate artefacts, not by themselves an observable difference between models — and on the geocentrist's own Machian reading those very terms are real gravitomagnetic fields sourced by a rotating cosmos, so the line hands over the strongest reply in their repertoire.

The opening concession offers satellite navigation as an example of integrating the field equations in Earth-fixed rotating coordinates; the Fourth point then says GPS synchronises the whole constellation in the Earth-Centred Inertial frame precisely because the rotating frame will not close. Failure scenario: a defender pairs the two and says we cannot keep our story straight — either navigation does its physics in the rotating frame, in which case the Sagnac argument is overstated, or it does not, in which case the concession's headline example is false. The reconciliation is real (GPS delivers ECEF coordinates but performs synchronisation in ECI, per Ashby, Living Reviews in Relativity 6:1, whose 207.4 ns figure I recomputed as 2ωA/c² = 2.074e−7 s) but it is not on the page — and the concession paragraph is the one that most needs to be unimpeachable, because its purpose is to establish that we do not overstate.
holes.recommendation: Replace with: “geodesy, VLBI and satellite navigation all deliver results in Earth-fixed coordinates as routine business — though, as the fourth point below shows, the rotating chart makes you pay for it with a synchronisation term, which is a cost and not a prohibition.”

holes.quoted_phrase: they are the Coriolis and centrifugal effects, and they are locally measurable
holes.description: scripts/deep_batch5.py:62. Off-diagonal components of the metric in a rotating chart are chart-dependent and are not themselves locally measurable; the same paragraph goes on to say so correctly (“It is not ‘the Earth-fixed chart is illegal’ … rotation relative to the local inertial structure is a coordinate-free invariant”). Failure scenario: this is the one sentence in an otherwise careful paragraph a physicist-defender can quote back as a category error, and because the cluster basis line makes the same mistake it will read as our real view rather than a slip. It also invites the standard Machian reply — on the geocentric reading those terms are genuine gravitomagnetic fields produced by the rotating cosmos, so measuring them settles nothing — which the paragraph's later formulation exists to pre-empt.
holes.recommendation: Replace with: “Those terms are not decoration; they are what the Coriolis and centrifugal effects look like in that chart. The chart components are not themselves measurable — but the invariant they encode is: the rotation of the Earth relative to the local compass of inertia.”

holes.quoted_phrase: A permission has been promoted to a demonstration without a word being altered.

It happens in Sungenis and Bennett, who restate the covariance point affirmatively rather than as a concession; the list then inherits the assertion and drops the founder's qualification with it. reviews.summary: R01's substantive refutation is the strongest thing on the page and survives every attack I could mount: the covariance concession is total and correct, the (a)-chart-change / (b)-physical-model equivocation is the right crux, the KERNEL steelman is genuinely at kernel tier (Kretschmann plus Bouw's own concession, both conceded outright), and the hedge rule is satisfied — the argument is answered at van der Kamp's strength, not the list's. The page also stays inside the hard constraints: it reports that Bouw refers the decision to Scripture without adjudicating Scripture, and makes no motive, finance or bad-faith claim about Sungenis, Bennett, DeLano or anyone else. What does not survive is the packaging. One critical citation error: the Galileo Was Wrong source label says Vol. I (2006) while the scan it links is Volume II, 7th ed., 2013, chs 7-13 — stale against our own published finding at ARG-E03, and it carries five quotations including the ones attributing a preferred-frame ether theory to living authors. One major self-contradiction: the cluster basis line renders directly above the refutation and runs the exact SURFACE argument our own steelman marks "do not use", which the refutation then disowns two sentences later. One major provenance gap: eight items are dated to a 1968 booklet nobody has read while every quotation comes from the 1988 book — the fourth instance of the failure mode already logged three times in corrections.json. Three moderates (a GPS-frame self-contradiction between the first and fourth paragraphs, a category error about chart components being "locally measurable", and a compression note that blames the list for an upgrade the gloss attributes to Sungenis and Bennett) and two minors. Verdict STANDARD PHYSICS holds; nothing here changes the conclusion, but the citation and the basis line are both things a defender can use to discredit the site.

reviews.hedge_rule_note: PASS, and this entry is one of the better applications of the rule on the board. Side by side: the list gives fifteen bare noun phrases ("Metric tensors Earth-centered", "Noether charges Earth-defined", "Renormalization frame Earth lab"); the source gives one sentence — "any reasonable coordinate system may be used. The weave pattern of a net does not determine the shape of the objects that are put into it." The refutation opens by conceding that sentence is correct, answers it on the merits with the two-edged Kretschmann objection (if covariance has no physical content it has none to lend geocentrism), and only then reaches the item titles, explicitly labelled "addressed to the items, whose author we do not know". Drift verdict drifted=True / unsourced_addition is right and is not being used to avoid work — it is backed by an actual term search. BUT the scope of that search is mislabelled throughout (see holes 1-3): the search was run over the archive scan, and the scan is Volume II of the 7th edition (2013), chs 7-13 — not "Vol. I (2006)", which our passage, sources entry, straw_man block, compression note and cluster record all say. The hedge-rule reasoning survives; the citation attached to it does not.

WebFetch of the archive item cited in our own sources block (GalileoWasWrongTheChurchSungenisRobertA.Bennett4276) returns front matter reading Volume II, Seventh edition, 2013, chapters 7 to 13 — which is also the standing finding recorded in scripts/_b7_C07.py, where our own batch-7 pass confirmed that the rotating-frame Lagrangian at p. 161 and the close of the General covariance section at p. 171 both land inside that Vol. II scan. We have not established which volume carried these chapters in the pre-2013 arrangement.

holes.quoted_phrase: whose off-diagonal terms in an Earth-fixed chart are the Coriolis and centrifugal effects the authors themselves derive
holes.description: Wrong physics, in the field readers see first, and repeated twice more in the body (steelman: “Write the metric in an Earth-fixed rotating chart and it acquires off-diagonal time–angle components… They are the Coriolis and centrifugal effects”; refutation: “Those are not bookkeeping. They are the Coriolis and centrifugal effects”). In the rotating (Langevin) metric the off-diagonal g_tφ = ωr² term yields the Coriolis force; the centrifugal force comes from the radial gradient of the time–time component g_tt = −(1 − ω²r²/c²) at order ω². The entry knows this elsewhere — the Kind 5 paragraph correctly attributes the (1 − ω²r²/c²) factor to g_tt when it derives the light cylinder — so the page contradicts itself on the same metric two paragraphs apart. A GR-literate defender scores a cheap point on the one paragraph where we claim technical authority.
holes.recommendation: TLDR: “What distinguishes a rotating Earth is not the coordinate labels but the dynamical metric, which in an Earth-fixed chart acquires an off-diagonal time-angle term (Coriolis) and an altered time-time term (centrifugal) — the same terms the authors themselves derive.” Body (steelman and refutation, both places): “Write the metric in an Earth-fixed rotating chart and it acquires an off-diagonal time–angle component and an altered time–time component. Those are not bookkeeping. They are the Coriolis and centrifugal effects respectively, and they are measured:”

holes.quoted_phrase: since there the distant stars traverse their circuits once a day and those beyond r = c/ω move superluminally
holes.description: This sentence undoes the two sentences before it. We have just told the reader that coordinate velocities in a non-inertial chart are not bounded by c and that only locally measured velocities are — then we argue against the geocentric model from coordinate speeds exceeding c. The word “physically” is carrying the whole load and is never unpacked, and the standard geocentrist reply is exactly the one our own R05 exists to handle: if the entire mass-energy of the universe rotates, it drags the local inertial frames with it, so no star exceeds c locally and the light cylinder objection presupposes a global inertial frame the model denies. Our own advocate.preemptive states the correct version of this point (a physically rotating shell “needs a dynamical account of what holds the shell together at those radii”); the refutation body states the weaker, self-contradicting version.
holes.recommendation: And the direction of the difficulty matters. The point is not that coordinate speeds above c are forbidden — we have just said they are not — but that a universe which physically rotates about a stationary Earth is a different claim from a relabelling, and it owes a dynamical account: what sources the rotation, and what state of motion the distant matter is in relative to its own local inertial frames out beyond r = c/ω. Answering “the rotating universe drags those frames with it” is available, and it is answered at R05; what it costs is the claim that the model differs observationally from the standard one at all. The standard picture incurs no such debt, because in it nothing is rotating that needs holding.

holes.quoted_phrase: rather than volume I, which we have not yet resolved

Leaving the open question standing here means the page tells the reader two different things about the same document, and it weakens a finding that is in fact firmer than we say.

(b) “All one argument” is what the refutation explicitly denies: it sorts the items into five kinds, three of which are not restatements of coordinate freedom at all but an imported term (gauge), terms whose content runs the other way (Noether, symmetry breaking) and an equivocation (renormalization scale). The core sentence is Sungenis and Bennett's and is correct; six of the vocabularies are not located in the volume we could search and are not shown to be theirs. Answered at R01."; real_source="General covariance; Kretschmann's 1917 objection"; originator_work="Galileo Was Wrong, Vol. I (core claim); the scanned text searched is Vol. II, 7th ed. 2013".

The hedge rule's second clause says the gap between list and source is a finding to publish, not a caveat to bury in paragraph six; and the harness says an error of prominence in a TLDR outranks the same error further down.

citation_failures: Passage locator and sources label both give “Galileo Was Wrong Vol. I (2006)” for the archive scan GalileoWasWrongTheChurchSungenisRobertA.Bennett4276 — WebFetch of that scan returns front matter reading Volume II, Seventh edition, 2013, chapters 7 to 13.
